records: The Ceremonial Knife and the Sun-Crest Sheath... It's uncanny how closely their sizes match. They look as though they belong together.

Preserve the matching dimensions and tentative pairing; use the exact registered item titles. One legacy rendering of this line was incidentally exposed by a terminology search after its clean meaning was saved; this draft is grounded in the complete Japanese exchange.
Indeed... Perhaps they did, once.
Gerhard agrees cautiously with Hodram's suggestion; do not turn the possible original pairing into an established fact.
Then let's try putting the knife in the sheath... What!?
Preserve inserting the knife and the abrupt surprise; no invented unsheathing action.
Whoa! What's happening!?
Gerhard reacts to the unexplained event with an immediate exclamation.
Light... from the sheath? Argh, it's so bright I can't keep my eyes open!
Keep the source of the light and inability to keep his eyes open; do not invent an image projected elsewhere.
What on earth just happened...?
Hodram is still trying to understand the event, rather than announcing a solution.
Look at the blade! A pattern has appeared on it...
Gerhard directs attention to the newly visible blade pattern, not a wall or the sheath's decoration.
Incredible... This must be a map to the New World's Proof of Supremacy. Though how it appeared is beyond me...
Preserve the probable map interpretation and unexplained phenomenon; use the established Proof term without claiming the Proof itself was acquired.
Someone said they'd be waiting for you in Alexandria.
Keep the unidentified person's message and location; do not supply a name or relationship.
Alexandria...?
Preserve Hodram's questioning repetition of the destination.
You're with {MACRO:FO}. All right, go through.
Preserve the exact faction macro and permission to pass; add no affiliation or rank beyond the source.
You who rule the Mediterranean, I bestow this upon you.
The officiant's ceremonial address is deliberately formal; add no religion or additional office.
Who are you...?
Preserve Hodram's unfinished inquiry into the stranger's identity.
Someone who has long resisted Ottoman rule.
The speaker identifies a history of resistance, not a named order, military rank or biography.
Then... were you the one who helped Sera and the others?
Keep the inference as a question and include the other escapees; the following reply declines details.
There's no need to concern yourself with the details. Now, decipher it and find the Proof without delay.
Preserve the evasive answer and urgency to solve the clue; the Proof has not yet been found.
There are others who escaped Ottoman rule, as we did. Look for the ruins in Turkey.
Retain both the other escapees and the stated location; do not invent who owns or inhabits the ruins.
The Patterned Cloth... There's no doubt it's a map to the Mediterranean's Proof of Supremacy, but...
Hodram is certain of the cloth's purpose while its map remains unreadable; use the registered item name.
It certainly doesn't look like a map as it is.
Gerhard comments on the present appearance, leaving room for the proposed heat-reveal solution.
Maybe we're supposed to use that Brass Lamp. Invisible ink, perhaps...?
Charles suggests a heat-revealed message tentatively; this is one conditional crew alternative, not consecutive advice from both crew members.
Hey, why don't we try warming it over the Brass Lamp?
Yifa offers the alternate heat-reveal suggestion in a more casual voice; do not describe burning the cloth.
Let's try it. I'll warm the cloth over the lamp...
Preserve the trial and heating action without inventing destruction or a separate item-use instruction.
Oh!
Retain Gerhard's brief surprise as the map appears.
It worked!
Charles celebrates the success of his suggestion; keep this distinct from Yifa's alternate response.
Well done, Charles. Now we have a map to the Mediterranean's Proof of Supremacy.
Retain the named praise and acquisition of a map, not the Proof itself.
Called it!
Yifa's playful satisfaction localizes the drawn-out celebratory expression, contrasting with Charles's straightforward reaction.
Well done, Yifa. Now we have a map to the Mediterranean's Proof of Supremacy.
Keep the conditional praise paired with Yifa's suggestion and the exact same map outcome.
Oh, {MACRO:FA}, have you heard?
Preserve the name macro while expressing the port worker's conversational lead-in naturally; add no title.
Apparently, a new town has sprung up here on the Black Sea.
Preserve recent founding as reported news, not a personally witnessed event or a different sea.
Oh? What's it called?
Keep Hodram's interested question simple and conversational.
Abhaz... I think that was it.
Use the current source-bound town label Abhaz and retain the worker's uncertainty; broader place-name review is not newly approved.
Abhaz... Can't say I've heard of it.
Gerhard has not heard the town name before; this does not establish that the surrounding country is unknown.
Preserve Sera's brief nonverbal recognition before Hodram notices it.
What is it, Sera?
Hodram responds to her reaction without assuming he already understands its cause.
{MACRO:FI}... Take me to that town...
Keep the captain-name macro and Sera's halting, earnest request; do not make her language suddenly fluent.
Of course. Do you know something about it?
Hodram agrees readily, then asks about her knowledge; avoid an invented objection or condition.
My country... Everyone is building it again...
Preserve the homeland and rebuilding in Sera's hesitant voice; no royal status is stated in this exchange.
Wait... Is that where you're from?
Hodram infers that this is her homeland rather than asserting an already established identity.
(Nods.)
Retain the source's nonverbal confirmation without adding spoken English.
I see... Your people are building a town back home.
Keep her people's rebuilding at home; do not invent an army, royal retinue or new political structure.
If it's on the Black Sea, it shouldn't be far from here. Come on, Sera. Let's go.
Preserve the tentative distance inference and warm decision to depart, without adding travel time or route mechanics.
Yes!
Sera's short, eager acceptance closes the exchange; no unsupported form of address is added.
